pr_title: Revert the LIFX discovery interface selection changes
pr_body:
## Proposed change

This resolves the broken discovery that occurred since the release
of 2022.5 when the interface selection was limited to interfaces
enable in Home Assistant's configuration, rather than all interfaces
on which LIFX devices were discovered.

The inflight controls are still in place, which will prevent duplicate
discoveries or existing unique_id errors.

Signed-off-by: Avi Miller <me@dje.li>

pr_comments: Being a `CODEOWNER` for an internal integration that has no tests that uses a practically abandoned library is not for me. This PR also removes me from the LIFX integration.
Sorry to hear you want to drop codeownership based on a code review; which I think was reasonable, mature and open towards you and towards keeping Home Assistant best design practices in check.

It wasn't your code review that made me drop ownership: I can't take the stress of being pinged by all the GitHub issues being opened due to changes in discovery that I can't fix without either breaking the architecture rules or properly rewriting the entire integration to replace aiolifx.

For the history, @frenck is right, we decided to handle it like he said: https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/discussions/509

If you dislike that, please open a new architecture issue. Having an integration deal with the network is a bad design and hard to handle and maintain for us.

Thank you @Djelibeybi ❤️ 

That is much appreciated!

../Frenck

> It wasn't your code review that made me drop ownership: I can't take the stress of being pinged by all the GitHub issues being opened due to changes in discovery that I can't fix without either breaking the architecture rules or properly rewriting the entire integration to replace aiolifx.

I think if we refactor the integration like we did with tplink to use HA's internals for retries / device management it will make things a lot easier to maintain per my comment here https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/72213#issuecomment-1152618333

I'll work on that after https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/74290 is wrapped up. @Djelibeybi hopefully you'll consider keeping codeowner once its in a maintainable state.

> @Djelibeybi hopefully you'll consider keeping codeowner once its in a maintainable state.

Nah, I think I'll keep working on my custom integration that uses Photons instead. It's clear that I don't understasnd Home Assistant's internals well enough for this.

issue_context.title: Automatically onboarding DiscoveryFlows breaks  LIFX discovery
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The addition of https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/73841 has broken the LIFX integration discovery for any non-default or non-standard network configuration.

This is pretty simple to replicate too: run Home Assistant 2022.7.0 or later on a host with two NICs, with the default NIC connected to a different subnet than any LIFX bulbs but enable mDNS propagation to that subnet. Home Assistant will enable the LIFX integration automatically, but no bulbs are discovered until the interface on the same subnet as the LIFX devices is enabled in the configuration.

Discovery flow is ignoring the actual function used for discovery, so it's registering false positives. 

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.7.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2022.6.7

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Core

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

Discovery flow should still run the specified function to ensure that the triggered auto-discovery actually results in finding devices on the network as currently configured.
comments:
This is actually already an issue, as the apparently LIFX needs validation, but doesn't right now because it's using the discovery flow.

IMHO this is not an issue resulting from #73841 what you describe can already happen if e.g., mDNS is relayed, but HA can't access the network (in general, regardless of which phase).

If being able to connect is a concern, it should validate that before actually creating the config entry. 

Linked issue #74246 is not related, as #73841 only happens during onboarding, while #74246 is about upgrading (in which a user would already have been onboarded and thus requires confirmation like before).

review_comments:
We should only scan on Home Assistant-enabled interfaces.

We really need to limit down on trying to resolve advanced network use cases. Trying to resolve those, will always end up in weird behavior and other things; while the root cause, 99% of the time, is misconfiguration by the end-user.

If one runs an advanced network setup, dealing with things resulting from that: is an end-user problem.

That would be a lovely idea, but no-one knows about Home Assistant's network configuration  and the change to restrict scanning has just caused issues without solving any problems.

The actual problem of avoiding duplicate discoveries and non-unique ID errors is still solved in this instance.

>  but no-one knows about Home Assistant's network configuration

That is not an integration issue to solve.


The reason I start responding now on this, is that is another change (after many others) around network interface, discovery and multiple interfaces.

This is not a concern we want to deal with, it only leads to problems and is something we don't do anywhere else either.

Other integrations deal with the same problems; none of them are struggling with them or trying to work around the issues.

It is just odd, the advanced network configurations should not be a HA concern. It's an end-user concern. From our perspective (at the integration level), it should ignore that and (at best) make use of the network information provided.
It's not my problem to solve either, so I vote with restoring the LIFX functionality until someone else decides how to solve it.

> It's not my problem to solve either

I'm sorry, I don't mean to be harsh, we are trying to solve issue here. And having discussions about it and following general design rules and principles around that, sounds like a normal thing to do to me.

This is your PR right? It seems like you try to solve a problem, and I'm jumping into the review process. I'm happy to help, discuss and getting things somewhere. But it seems like you are not interested (for whatever reason).

Anyways, tried to find more information for you on the subject: <https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/discussions/509>

Just in case you wondered about more context.

If I'd written the integration in the first place, I'd be committed to fixing it. And the custom integration I'm working on follows the rules.

As this is a built in integration, I think the core developers should fix this. This PR is my recommendation in the interim until that happens.
